title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: Microsoft Learn now documents an administrator-created auto-labeling policy for applying library defaults to existing files, contrary to the briefing's statements that the mechanism, default and control are undocumented. Published licensing guidance also covers this service-side labeling scenario.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans automatic labeling of existing SharePoint files using their document library's default sensitivity label without manual user labeling.
claims.quote: Enables auto‑labeling of existing SharePoint files to match the default sensitivity label configured on their document library.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: The default is unknown because Microsoft has not said whether labeling existing files requires administrator action.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to admin-opt-in. Replace the repeated default-state gap with: 'Learn documents an administrator-created auto-labeling policy to extend library defaults to eligible existing files; review simulation results before turning on the policy. The roadmap still targets GCC, GCC High and DoD for December CY2026.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe applying default library sensitivity labels to existing files.
claims.quote: ### Apply default sensitivity labels from SharePoint document libraries to existing files
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this change' with: 'Learn describes applying library defaults to existing files through an auto-labeling policy, while the separate library-default page still lists existing files at rest as a limitation of that library setting.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically to sources; retain the government-cloud roadmap status and target.

claims.claim: The existing library-default feature labels new uploads and edited existing files when they are unlabeled or carry a lower-priority label.
claims.quote: any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied if they don't already have a sensitivity label, or they have a sensitivity label but with lower priority.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: For the documented library-default setting, a lower-priority label is overridden unless it was applied manually.
claims.quote: Default sensitivity label for a document library: Location-based labeling, applicable only for SharePoint. Overrides a lower-priority label unless manually applied.

claims.claim: The cited library-default page lists existing files at rest as a limitation.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to existing files at rest in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label encryption can change who can open a file.
claims.quote: When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted, so that it: Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels to sources for the statement about encryption restricting who can open files.
